claim.quote: No candidate for the stellar core collapse has been detected during the observation period.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published Astropart. Phys. (DOI 10.1016/j.astropartphys.2019.102404 on the arXiv record).

key_value_text.quote: An upper bound of the mean frequency of core collapse supernovae in our Galaxy is 0.070 year
key_value_text.value: No core-collapse candidate in 33.02 years of observation (30 June 1980 to 31 December 2018); upper bound 0.070 per year (90 % CL) on the mean frequency of core-collapse supernovae in the Galaxy

name: Supernova Neutrino Burst Monitor at the Baksan Underground Scintillation Telescope

summary.plain: For over 33 years the Baksan telescope has watched for the burst of neutrinos from a star exploding in our Galaxy. It has seen none, which limits such explosions to fewer than about one per fourteen years.
summary.technical: Neutrino-burst monitor with a 240 t target: observation time 33.02 yr (1980-06-30 to 2018-12-31), no core-collapse candidate; upper bound 0.070 per year (90 % CL) on the mean Galactic core-collapse supernova frequency.

title: Supernova Neutrino Burst Monitor at the Baksan Underground Scintillation Telescope
why_it_matters: A continuous, decades-long watch for Galactic supernova neutrinos; the same instrument recorded neutrinos from SN 1987A.
